overall: The AG found the Carver Board of Selectmen did not violate the Open Meeting Law. Three members who formed a subcommittee met separately with the Planning Director, and the AG credited the Board's account that they did not deliberate as a group. The AG added an unraised reminder about quorum communications, with no finding and no order.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged a quorum of the Board met privately and discussed and voted on a nuisance/blight warrant article (Article #20) outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we find that the Board did not deliberate outside of a noticed meeting.

allegations.summary: AG raised on its own that the Planning Director's April 5 email to all subcommittee members may have relayed individual members' views to a quorum; not raised in the complaint.
allegations.key_passage: We remind the Board that communications that reach a quorum of members and include the opinions of those members on a matter within the body’s jurisdiction is deliberation, even if no public body member responds.
